text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English astronomer and mathematician, EDMOND HALLEY, who was the first to realise that comets did not appear randomly, was born in 1656. HALLEY's comet was named after him.

English pioneer motor car engineer BARON HERBERT AUSTIN was born in 1866. He started his career making shearing machines in Australia and ended up being chairman of the Wolseley company, which also made motor cars.
The Belgian/Tasmanian Antarctic explorer LOUIS BERNACCI was born in 1876. He was the first Australian to work in the Antarctica. SCOTT was best man at his wedding.
The woman who created Scarlett O'Hara, MARGARET MITCHELL, was born in 1900 in Atlanta.
South African surgeon and heart transplant pioneer CHRISTIAAN BARNARD was born in 1922.

American singer PATTI PAGE (CLARA ANN FOWLER) was born in 1927. Her hits included "How Much Is That Doggie In The Window?" (1953) and "Hush, Hush, Sweet Charlotte" (1965). In the 1950s she sold more records than any other singer. From 1955 to 1958 she had her own television show.

U.S. singer and songwriter MINNIE RIPERTON was born in 1948. After singing backing for several artists such as JOHNNY NASH and STEVIE WONDER she started her solo career and had a hit with "Lovin' You" in 1975. MINNIE died in 1979.
American singer and songwriter RICKY LEE JONES, who made her first record in 1979, was born in 1954. "Chuck E.'s In Love" was a hit. In the late eighties she produced an album "Flying Cowboys".
American child film star and teen-idol LEIF GARRETT was born in 1961. His singing hits included "Surfin' USA" and "Run-around Sue" (1977) and "I Was Made For Dancin'" (1978).
** EVENTS **
1793 : The revolutionary French government allowed the
public to see the royal art collection in the Louvre for the first time.
1880 : The internationally famous French actress SARAH
BERNHARDT gave her first performance in New York.
1932 : Democrat FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT swept to power
defeating sitting Republican president HERBERT HOOVER. ROOSEVELT had promised a "New Deal" which included increased public spending on railways, roads,and farming and unemployment benefits.
1939 : Seven people were killed and more than 60 were
injured when a bomb exploded in Munich shortly after HITLER had left. He had just given his speech on the anniversary of his abortive Beer Hall putsch.
1952 : South African police opened fire on rioters,
killing 14 blacks and wounding 39.
1955 : Australia's one millionth post-war migrant BARBARA
PORRITT of Yorkshire was welcomed by Federal Immigration Minister HAROLD HOLT.
1968 : One of the Great Train Robbery suspects BRUCE
REYNOLDS was arrested.
1972 : East and West Germany agreed to normalise
relations.
1987 : A man serving 17 years for murder in a Californian
prison sued a juror for 24 million dollars for sleeping during the trial. The man claimed the sleeping juror contributed towards his "incorrect conviction".
1989 : In Virginia, DOUGLAS WILDER became the first black
state governor in the United States.
1994 : Transport Unions around the country lodged claims
for a 15 percent pay-rise, threatening industrial action over Christmas if the claim wasn't approved.
